I don't have a question, but I am going to help you out a little bit on your title. Please know I'm not correcting you to be a jerk, but rather I hope this will help you speak English better!

The biggest problem is the subject/verb agreement. The subject is singular ("I"), but in your sentence the verb is plural ("do"). Instead, you should use the singular form of the verb, "does." Next, I know this is intuitive, but when describing someone's age as an adjective, you use the singular form of "year." So, "I am a 15 year old boy..." Your version would be correct if you were describing your age in the predicate (i.e., "I am 15 years old.").

Now put it all together, and you've got "I am a 15 year old boy who does home-school." This is technically correct, although it would sound a little wooden to a native speaker. We don't "do," school, we "go to" school. While I realize that you don't actually "go" anywhere because you have school in your home, we still use the common phrase "go" in reference to home-school. So a perfect version of your sentence would be, "I am a 15 year old boy who goes to home-school."

You've stated that you study 'whatever you want'. The idea of school is not to learn, but to be taught how to learn and possibly some basics of certain subjects. Why have you chosen/ have your parents chosen to homeschool you?
